rule: Sound becomes a horde signal (volume minus weather attenuation, zero below a floor, divided by 12 per submap, floored at 8 and capped at 180, further divided underground). Each idle group within signal minus submap distance gets the noise origin as its destination and a tracking budget of (signal minus distance) times 12 ticks. A later signal only raises a tracking budget, never lowers it. A tracking group spends one tracking tick per turn, earns energy equal to its speed each turn, and spends 100 energy per tile step; it stops at zero budget or at the destination. Idle groups never move, because the roam/city wander function and the monster-alert path have no callers. A single hunter (the Hunted trait) steps once per 2.5 game minutes; each attempt succeeds with the terrain divisor (road 1, field 3, forest/swamp/bridge 6, river 10, other 25) times a speed roll, and steps one king-move toward the player's area, which is re-targeted by a one-in-120 per-turn roll. Each hunter death increments a global iteration counter, which reduces hits taken per damage type and raises speed about one percent per iteration for 1000 seconds. The survive variant respawns a new hunter 40-80 overmap tiles away on field terrain after each death; the trait's kill variant ends the trait instead. Scheduled reveals run from a per-turn timed-event queue: each entry has a per-turn hook and an actualize step when due; some entries hold, telegraph, self-reschedule, or chain. Dying groups lose one fifth of their population per day with integer division.

keep: Sound as a pull, not an alarm: distance-scaled tracking budget, quieter sounds never shorten a pull.
Terrain-weighted hunter: road fast, open ground slow, retarget by roll, so the chase is a fact of the world.
Escalation per death with a global counter that is a character-level number.
Hold-until-condition timed events, telegraphed reveals, and self-rescheduling spread events.
Chained timed events: one trigger schedules the next after a delay.
change: Hop-based zone distance instead of submap distance.
Per-tick budget for group steps (donor has a TODO for it).
Time-based decay instead of integer fifth-per-day.
Cap the per-kill hit reduction so the hunter stays killable.

Fix defects 1-7 (reinforcement call has no handler; hunter wounds lost on despawn; energy bank while blocked; groups dropped when the target overmap is not in memory; dead wander/alert path; linear timed-event lookup (noted only); SPAWN_WYRMS hold uses the wrong sign).
Reinforcement call becomes a server event with at most three attackers engaged at once (MAX_ATTACKERS = 3).
look_test: Target file src/fight/pursuit.ts (new module), row 4 (fight loop: aggro, chase, leash). On a phone-width 3x3 zone map with a road cross, fields and forest: advance 2.5 minutes forty times and watch the hunter stay still on dirt, creep on fields and sprint on the road; then shout from distance and from close and watch the six idle tokens' tracking bar extend but never shrink; then kill the hunter and watch it return one point less damage per hit and slightly faster. Pass when the hunter reads from a glance at 375 wide, the shout reads as a pull, and a repeat kill reads as harder without a wall of numbers.
